prolfqua: Proteomics Label Free Quantification

Source: R/prolfqua-package.R
prolfqua-package.Rd

Covers the steps of a mass spectrometry based label-free quantification (LFQ) analysis: quality control, normalization, aggregation of peptides to proteins, modelling, hypothesis testing and sample size estimation. A single function, build_contrast_analysis(), fits a model per protein and computes contrasts with one of many methods: linear, robust and rank-based regression, 'limma' and 'limma'-voom, 'DEqMS' variance moderation, the detection probability model of 'limpa', Firth logistic and binomial models of detection, mixed models and a median-peptide test derived from ROPECA on peptide-level data, a hurdle model combining intensity and detection, and variants that impute groups without observations at the limit of detection. All methods return their results through the same interface and columns, so they can be compared and combined. Models simple designs with one explanatory variable as well as experiments with several factors. Intended for proteomics core facilities and researchers analysing protein or peptide intensities quantified with MaxQuant, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, FragPipe or similar software. Developed while analysing dozens of proteomics datasets at the Functional Genomics Center Zurich.

Audience

Proteomics core facilities and researchers analysing label-free protein or peptide intensities quantified with MaxQuant, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, FragPipe or similar software: quality control, normalization, aggregation, differential expression and sample size estimation.

Benchmarks

The performance claims of Wolski et al. (2023, J Proteome Res), comparing prolfqua's methods with MSstats, msqrob2 and proDA on benchmark datasets, are reproduced by the vignettes of the companion package prolfquabenchmark (https://prolfqua.github.io/prolfquabenchmark/).

Resources

Approximate figures, measured on simulated data with 12 to 48 samples on one laptop; times scale with the machine.

  • Memory: the long table takes about 75 bytes per row (one feature in one sample). setup_analysis() needs about 8 times that for a short time, because it completes the feature by sample grid, adding NA rows for absent combinations.

  • Matrix backends (limma, limma_impute, limma_voom, limma_voom_impute, deqms_voom, limpa) analyse 5,000 to 10,000 proteins in about a second or less; limpa_nested, which also aggregates, takes about 1.5 s per 1,000 proteins.

  • Per-subject backends fit one model per protein or peptide on a single thread, contrasts included: about 1 ms per protein for lm, 1 ms per peptide for the ROPECA methods, 5 ms per protein for hurdle_nested and 10 to 16 ms for lmer_nested, which is two to three minutes at 10,000 proteins.

  • Aggregation of peptides to proteins takes about 1 ms per protein with median polish and with rlm. The QC writers take about 0.1 s (write_plots()) and 0.2 s (write_boxplots()) per protein, one page each; write_plots(subset = ) limits their cost.

  • Per-subject backends keep every fitted model (about 9 KB per protein for lm, 40 KB for lmer_nested), so that predict(), residuals() and vcov() work on the analysis.

  • null_split_check() repeats the whole analysis n_splits times (default 20); n_features limits its cost.

Options

prolfqua.verbose

TRUE (default) or FALSE. With FALSE, prolfqua prints no informative messages, such as columns added, rows removed or files written. Warnings and errors are not affected. The messages carry class prolfqua_message, so an application can route them to its own log with withCallingHandlers(prolfqua_message = ...).

prolfqua.progress

Progress reporting while models and contrasts are computed per protein: NULL (default) shows a terminal progress bar, "message" a throttled message with elapsed time, and a function(i, total, label) is called with the progress.

Missing and non-finite values

An NA intensity is a missing observation. The method argument of build_contrast_analysis decides how missing observations are handled: dropped per fit (e.g. lm, limma), imputed at the limit of detection (the _impute methods), or modelled as detection (firth, binomial_nested, hurdle_nested); impute_from_model fills them from fitted models. The log, log2 and log10 transforms turn zero intensities (not detected) into NA. Fitting and aggregation stop with a classed error on Inf, -Inf or NaN intensities (prolfqua_error_nonfinite_response), on NA in hierarchy, factor or sample columns (prolfqua_error_missing_key), and on inputs without rows (prolfqua_error_bad_argument). A subject whose residual variance is zero (constant or noiseless response) keeps its estimated difference, but its test statistics are NA, with a prolfqua_zero_variance warning, and it is left out of the variance moderation prior.

Input types and conversion

LFQData$new() accepts a long table as data.frame, tibble or data.table and stores it as a tibble. The response must be numeric; it is stored as a plain double, without extra classes or attributes such as I(), units or labels (announced). In setup_analysis, factor columns stay factors, so their level order sets the reference level of the design; ordered factors become unordered and unused levels are dropped (announced). Numeric, logical or Date factor columns become character labels (announced), whose reference level is the first sorted label. Hierarchy columns are used by their labels. List columns holding the response or a hierarchy, factor or sample column are refused with a prolfqua_error_bad_argument; other list columns are dropped by setup. Single-valued arguments (flags, counts, seeds, probabilities) must have length one; counts must be whole numbers and are converted to integer.

Provenance

Each LFQData, model and analysis records the problems and dropped items that happen in it; $provenance() returns them as a table (step, event, count, IDs, reason). Recorded are values set to NA (remove_small_intensities(), zeros in log transforms), removed rows, features and proteins (remove_decoys(), remove_contaminants(), filter_proteins_by_peptide_count()), estimation warnings in aggregation (e.g. rlm not converging), failed, warned, singular and LOD-refit fits, missing responses dropped per fit and, for an analysis, the subjects absent from the contrasts with the reason. Each step reports its new entries once: failures as one warning of class prolfqua_fit_failed, everything else as one prolfqua_message, which prolfqua.verbose = FALSE silences. Derived data (transformed, subset, rows removed) continues the record of its input; aggregated data and models start their own.

Lifecycle

prolfqua is stable. Its exported API follows the Bioconductor deprecation cycle: a renamed or removed interface calls .Deprecated() for one release before calling .Defunct() in a subsequent release. Changes affecting analyses are recorded in NEWS.

Glossary

LFQData

A long-format measurement table together with its AnalysisConfiguration; each row describes a feature in a sample.

AnalysisConfiguration

The mapping from table columns to hierarchy identifiers, sample identifiers, categorical factors and the response.

Hierarchy and hierarchy depth

Ordered measurement levels, such as protein, peptide and precursor. Depth selects the levels identifying a modelled subject; deeper levels identify its child features.

subject_id

The identifier columns of a modelled subject, usually one protein or a protein-peptide pair.

Factor

An explanatory variable defining experimental groups. setup_analysis() converts configured predictors to character labels, including numeric and ordered-factor inputs; numeric covariates and ordered-factor contrasts are not preserved through this setup.

Response

The numeric intensity column selected by the configuration, usually log2 abundance for modelling. On this scale a difference of one corresponds to a twofold abundance ratio.

Contrast

A named linear combination of group means or coefficients, for example treatment minus control.

linfct

A matrix with one row per requested linear function and one column per model coefficient. Multiplying it by the coefficient vector gives the estimates being tested.

Strategy

The formula, fitting algorithm and methods for extracting coefficients, residual variance, degrees of freedom and contrasts.

Model

Fitted regressions and their diagnostics, either per subject or in a matrix representation used by limma.

Facade

An analysis object composing a strategy, model and contrast calculation behind the same result and plotting interface.

Aggregated and nested input

Aggregated input has the same hierarchy keys as the output subject. Nested input also has child-feature keys; the analysis reports parent-level contrasts.

nr_children

The sample-wise number of measured child features, such as peptides used to estimate a protein intensity. It may be used as a fitting weight; DEqMS separately pools counts per protein.

LOD and imputation

The limit of detection on the working response scale, supplied explicitly or estimated from low-observation group means. Imputation replaces missing responses. The LOD methods refit otherwise unestimable subjects and borrow variance from successful fits.

estimate_type

A result label identifying how an estimate was obtained, for example from observed data or an imputed refit.

Moderation

Empirical Bayes shrinkage of residual variances towards a shared prior, optionally dependent on abundance or peptide count. Moderated degrees of freedom combine residual and prior information.

Null hypothesis and p-value

For a usual two-sided contrast test, the null states that the population contrast equals zero. Its p-value is the probability, assuming the null and model assumptions hold, of a statistic at least as extreme as the observed one. It is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true.

FDR

The false discovery rate: the expected proportion of false discoveries among rejected hypotheses. The default Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment is applied within contrast, assuming independent or suitably positively dependent tests. An adjusted p-value is not the probability that an individual protein is a false discovery.

Confidence interval

A range from a procedure with the stated repeated-sampling coverage under the model assumptions. Wald intervals use the estimated standard error and a t quantile; they do not assign a probability to a fixed parameter after observing the data.

Linear-model assumptions

On the working scale, classical linear models assume a linear mean, independent errors and constant residual variance; exact t inference also assumes normal errors. Weights allow specified relative variances and mixed models allow specified dependence within subjects. Outliers and heavy-tailed errors pull least-squares estimates; the robust methods rlm and rfit limit their influence. Robust, detection and imputation methods have different assumptions; diagnostics and the experimental design must guide the method choice.
